task: What is the minimum premium recorded in customers.csv?
notes: Single explicit numeric column, unambiguous statistic (minimum), not previously asked in any existing suite.

task: List every file currently available in the workspace.
notes: Trivial single-tool workspace listing task; not used as a primary task in any existing scenario file.

notes: find_duplicates targeting a non-customer_id column, explicitly named. No existing scenario names a duplicate-check column other than customer_id.

notes: filter_rows on a numeric-looking column (premium) rather than the city column used by every existing filter scenario.

task: In customers.csv, list the duplicate cities and the maximum age.
notes: Two-part explicit-column request: duplicates on city plus maximum (not average) age.

task: Give me the total premium and the number of columns in customers.csv.
notes: Combines a numeric total with a column-count question (count, not the list of columns as existing scenarios ask).

task: Tell me something about customers.csv.
notes: Fully open-ended request with no operation implied at all (not specifically an aggregate ask like existing ambiguous-summary scenarios).

task: Filter customers.csv by city.
notes: Filter column is given (city) but the value is missing -- a partial-information case, distinct from existing fully-unspecified filter scenarios.

task: Give me the statistics for our best customers in customers.csv.
notes: Both the selection criterion ("best") and the requested statistic are unspecified; no directly executable operation exists.

task: Convert customers.csv into a JSON file.
notes: No format-conversion tool exists; create_report producing a text file would not satisfy a JSON conversion request.

task: Split customers.csv into a separate file for each city.
notes: No tool can write new per-group files; filter_rows can select rows but cannot persist them as separate files.

task: For Hyderabad customers in customers.csv, tell me their total premium.
notes: calculate_summary always recomputes over the full file and cannot aggregate a filter_rows subset, so any call to it here would silently produce the wrong (whole-file) total presented as if it were the Hyderabad-only figure. This follows directly from the real tool contract, not an arbitrary V1 policy. Fresh city (Hyderabad) and statistic (total, not average) combination versus prior suites.

task: Preview the first five rows of orders.csv.
notes: orders.csv does not exist in the workspace; no existing missing-file scenario uses a preview request or this filename.

task: Calculate the average discount in customers.csv.
notes: "discount" is not a column in customers.csv and must not be silently mapped to premium or any other existing column.

task: Find duplicate values in the region column of customers.csv.
notes: "region" is not a column; tests invalid-column handling for find_duplicates rather than calculate_summary, which no existing scenario does.

task: Create a report for customers.csv.
notes: report_name is optional with a tool-level default; the filename is known, so no clarification is genuinely required. Existing report scenarios always supply an explicit report_name -- this is the complementary case.

task: Show the customers.csv row for customer CUST005.
notes: Filter column and value are both unambiguous even though phrased naturally; no existing scenario filters on customer_id.

task: In customers.csv, what is the maximum age?
notes: Fully unambiguous single-column, single-statistic request; minimum correct solution is exactly one calculate_summary call. No existing scenario asks for maximum age specifically.

task: In customers.csv, calculate the average premium and the average age.
notes: Two explicit, unambiguous columns requiring two calculate_summary calls; minimum useful tool count is exactly two. No existing scenario combines two independent averages in one request.
